Let's say we have a new, small community of no more than 100 people. Most families only really have enough to get by, however other families are quite well off (large houses, high-end technology, lots of food, etc.) The society already has everything it needs to function, although it is often expensive and not as efficient for the common man. Would it be ethical for the community to forcibly seize some of the more well-off families' wealth for the greater good of the community as a whole, (eg. with improved infrastructure, public education, health, etc.)?

What say ye, Voat?
Is Theft for the Greater Good of the Community Moral?

My answer:

Personally, I believe the wealthy should be forced to give up at least some of their wealth to their community for essentials such as infrastructure and law and order. We, as humans, are social creatures and function best when we cooperate - even if that means some people must be forced to comply. Besides, being wealthy doesn't necessarily make you're life all that much better, save for stress over money, because when you look at the big picture, you're just going to return back to the equilibrium. Being poor, however, can effect your wellbeing because you have to worry about money and will generally have a worse job, which can effect your happiness.

Not to mention, if it wasn't for the community, there would be no order, no infrastructure, no technology - at least not to the extent that we enjoy today. This are all things we have inherited. There wouldn't even be the system that allows them to become wealthy in the first place.

(tl;dr they should have to comply because we work best when we all cooperate and its generally more practical because it maximizes the wellbeing of society as a whole.)

Morality is subjective. Even if there's a god, that just defines morality as the rules that he came up with. Asking if something is ethical is asking if it's okay with me.

What do you want to accomplish? I assume you want a harmonious community. People have to agree. So we need to solve differences, to encourage people to agree and to have the same goals for the community. They have to have principles, because that's how you get humans to do things. This is usually done through religion and/or state propaganda.

Fascists typically want to create a harmonious community through nationalism, racial pride, and community racial homogeneity. This encourages bonding in the community, and a feeling of communal power and oneness. They agree on their community's (often harsh) rules.

More libertarian and anarchic goals emphasize people getting along and interacting only voluntarily. Despite any differences, they agree on everyone doing their own thing as long as it doesn't harm anyone else. Even if they have vastly different personal beliefs, they agree that this framework is the best way to live.

I mentioned these because they're seen as opposites. No matter what you do, it will only work if everyone agrees on it, because that's the definition of harmonious, the people getting along.

So how do you achieve that? Figure out what takes the least effort to get to, and get there? Unlikely, because you have personal beliefs and priorities, so you're going to want that sort of community. You can't escape being a piece of what you're trying to look down on. Neither can I.

But we, as a species, will eventually see the spread of whatever communities are best suited to spreading and outliving the ones that aren't. Evolution is a definition of something obvious and intrinsic.

We'll find out what happens. Even if the agreement is chemically induced by borg.
